summary: Jörg Heimbel is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Dorji Wangchuk and Franz-Karl Ehrhard and studied at Tibet University. His posts include positions at Hamburg, Göttingen, and Munich.
Jörg Plassen is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He has held professorships at Geumgang University and Ruhr University Bochum.

Jörundur Garðar Hilmarsson was a linguist specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned an M.A. from Oslo, studied at the Sorbonne, and completed his Ph.D. at Leiden, later teaching at the University of Iceland from around 1987 to 1992.

Jørn Borup was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Aarhus University under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader, and served as an associate professor there from around 2006 to 2023.

Júlia Szivák works in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Corvinus University, Eötvös Loránd University, Central European University, and Birmingham City University (PhD 2021). She held posts at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Nottingham.

Jürgen Hanneder is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn. He worked at the University of Bonn and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg before becoming a professor at Marburg in 2007.
Jürgen Neuß is an Indologist and historian who earned his PhD from the Free University of Berlin in 2007, where he studied under Harry Falk.

Jürgen Renn works in history, archaeology, and philosophy. After earning his Ph.D. at TU Berlin, he held posts at Boston University, the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science, and became Director at the Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology in 2022.

K. A. Nilakanta Sastri was a historian and Indologist who studied at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras. He held posts at Annamalai University, the University of Mysore, and served as Professor of Indian History and Archaeology at Madras (1929–1946).

K. A. Subramania Iyer was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Universities of London and Paris. He served as Professor and Sanskrit Department Head at Lucknow (1921–1960) and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
K. Ammini Amma is an Indology scholar who conducted research as a student at the University of Madras, attested in 1940 and 1971.
K. Balasubramania Iyer was an Indology scholar who served as Managing Editor of the Journal of Oriental Research and Secretary of the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute.
K. Jayakumar is an Indologist and linguist who studied at St. Joseph's Higher Secondary School, Thiruvananthapuram, and served in the Indian Administrative Service from around 1978 to 2012.
K. Kanapathypillai was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at Hartley College and the University of London between 1936 and 1940.

K. Kunjunni Raja was an Indologist and linguist who earned doctorates from the University of Madras and the University of London. In 1951, he became Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Madras.

K. L. Dhammajoti is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.A. from the University of Kelaniya. He held posts at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, University of Hong Kong, and University of Calgary.
K. Madhava Krishna Sarma was an Indologist who studied under C. Kunhan Raja. He was affiliated with the Adyar Library and Research Centre and served as Curator of the Anup Sanskrit Library.
K. Meenakshi is an Indologist and linguist who earned a PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964 under M. A. Mehendale, and later held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University.
K. Munirathnam is an Indologist and archaeologist who studied under N. S. Ramachandra Murthy and served as Director (Epigraphy) I/c at the Archaeological Survey of India.

K. N. Jayatilleke was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Cambridge under Ludwig Wittgenstein. He served as Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Ceylon from around 1958 to 1963.
